speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and were there any specific events or injuries preceding their onset?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's thumb (Stener lesion) involving the Ulnar Collateral Ligament of the 5th digit, or potentially a simple UCL tear given the mechanism of forceful abduction. Given the specific injury mechanism (jersey pull) and location (ring finger), a UCL tear is highly probable. I recommend obtaining X-rays to rule out avulsion fracture and then proceeding to MRI or Ultrasound for soft tissue evaluation. REQUEST TEST: Hand_X_Ray_RL; REQUEST IMAGES: Hand_Ultrasound.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
